To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The microbial communities in soils from an abandoned mining area were highly adapted to the metal-rich environment and showed a higher functional diversity in the most contaminated soils.

the structure and function of soil microbial communities at an abandoned mine site are determined by the amount of metal contamination, and that metal-contaminated soils have higher microbial evenness than non-contaminated soils.

the structure and function of microbial communities at an abandoned Pb- Zn mining site were affected by metal pollution and that taxa with high metabolic plasticities, as well as those with low tolerance to heavy metal contamination, were identified.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the adaptation of soil microbial communities and functions to metal contamination, and how these adaptations may contribute to the resilience of these communities to environmental stress.
the adaptation of soil microbial communities to metal contamination and how this adaptation may influence the structure and function of these microbial communities.
the effects of long-term metal contamination on soil microbial community structure, function, and the underlying mechanisms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the microbial community structure in the contaminated soils was shaped mainly by the metal concentration and the pH, whereas the microbial community composition was mainly determined by the amount of clay.
the structure and function of the microbial communities of the studied soils are highly adapted to metal contamination.

the microbial community structure is not only driven by metal contamination but also by other factors, including soil pH, clay content and the presence of specific taxa with high metabolic plasticities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
microbial communities are able to adapt to high metal concentrations and that the structure of the community changes with the contamination level.

microbial communities in highly polluted sites are characterized by higher evenness, higher abundance of taxa with high metabolic plasticities, and higher abundance of transcripts involved in metal resistance.

the microbial communities in the most contaminated samples are dominated by a high evenness of taxa with a high metabolic plasticity and that they express a higher amount of genes related to metal resistance mechanisms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
microbial communities can adapt to high levels of metals, but at the same time, their structure and function are strongly altered.
microbial communities in metal-contaminated soils are not only able to survive in the presence of metals, but also to adapt to the presence of these metals.
microbial communities in highly contaminated sites are more diverse and have a higher potential to adapt to metal contamination.
